Use the provided image as the exact visual reference for the singer, outfit, microphone, stage, composition, and comic-book art style. Use the provided 15-second audio clip as the sole performance and lip-sync reference.

A continuous 15-second live concert performance in a bold, hand-drawn comic-book style. The singer stands behind the fixed microphone at center stage, wearing the same orange-red pinstripe suit, black gloves, black waist belt, and elaborate golden beaded headpiece. Preserve the singer's facial features, body proportions, clothing details, microphone position, stage architecture, and the original image's dramatic red-and-amber lighting.

The singer performs the song with expressive, naturally synchronized mouth movements, following the timing, rhythm, phrasing, pauses, and emotional intensity of the supplied audio. The lips open, close, and form distinct singing shapes in response to the vocals. Facial expressions shift naturally between focused, soulful singing and confident, joyful engagement with the audience.

At the beginning, the singer faces the microphone and sings with an open, expressive mouth, shoulders gently moving to the beat. As the performance develops, the singer turns the head slightly from side to side, extends one gloved hand toward the audience, and opens both arms in an inviting gesture. During more emphatic vocal phrases, the singer points outward, lifts one hand near the face, and leans subtly toward the microphone. The hands move with musical intention rather than random waving. Between phrases, the singer relaxes the gestures and continues a gentle rhythmic sway. Toward the end, the singer delivers the final phrase with a stronger facial expression and an outward hand gesture.

Maintain the microphone as a stable physical object throughout the shot. The singer's mouth stays correctly aligned with the microphone when singing. Preserve natural hand anatomy and consistent character identity across every frame.

Camera: one uninterrupted medium shot, approximately waist-up, matching the reference image's frontal three-quarter perspective. Subtle handheld concert-camera movement with a very gentle cinematic push-in. No cuts, no sudden zooms, no camera orbit, no major reframing.

Visual style: premium illustrated concert animation, bold black ink contours, expressive hand-drawn linework, dense halftone shading, warm amber highlights, deep burgundy shadows, restrained red stage lighting, subtle animated light reflections on the golden headpiece. Preserve the original 2D comic-book aesthetic throughout; do not transform the character into photorealistic footage or a 3D animated model.

The performance must feel musically connected, emotionally convincing, fluid, and continuous, with believable singing articulation and coordinated head, shoulder, and hand movements.

No newly generated dialogue, no additional vocals, no background music replacement, no subtitles, no captions, no floating text, no logos, no scene transitions, no duplicated limbs, no facial distortion, no costume changes.
